title: search_all runs in serial and par_search_all on the rayon pool, both over any iterator of byte-like queries
body:
`SuffixArray::search_all` in `libsufr/src/lib.rs` at 6edc011 is

```rust
pub fn search_all<Q: AsRef<[u8]> + Sync>(&self, queries: &[Q]) -> Vec<Result<Hits<'_>>>
```

It runs the queries on the global rayon pool, logs the elapsed time with `info!`, and is called with `&[String]` from the CLI and `&[&str]` from the tests, which is the whole set of types the parameter serves. It came over from the `search-api` branch's `search_many` in 8022b6a without review.

## Proposal

Two functions with the same inputs. The serial one is the loop a caller would otherwise write; the parallel one runs on whatever rayon pool is current.

```rust
/// Search each query in turn, stopping at the first failed read.
pub fn search_all<Q>(&self, queries: impl IntoIterator<Item = Q>) -> Result<Vec<Hits<'_>>>
where
    Q: AsRef<[u8]>,
{
    queries.into_iter().map(|q| self.search(q.as_ref())).collect()
}

/// Search the queries on the current rayon pool, in the same order.
pub fn par_search_all<Q>(&self, queries: impl IntoIterator<Item = Q>) -> Result<Vec<Hits<'_>>>
where
    Q: AsRef<[u8]> + Sync,
{
    let queries: Vec<Q> = queries.into_iter().collect();
    queries.par_iter().map(|q| self.search(q.as_ref())).collect()
}
```

The parameter earns its place because `IntoIterator` plus `AsRef<[u8]>` covers every shape a caller has: `&[&str]`, `&[String]`, `&Vec<String>`, arrays, `Vec<&str>` and `Vec<String>` by value, any iterator with `Item = &str` or `String`, and the same shapes over `&[u8]`, `Vec<u8>` and `[u8; N]`. References work through the blanket `impl AsRef<U> for &T`.

Differences between the two:

| | `search_all` | `par_search_all` |
|---|---|---|
| bound on `Q` | `AsRef<[u8]>` | `AsRef<[u8]> + Sync` |
| the iterator | streamed | collected to a `Vec<Q>` first, since rayon parallelises slices |
| a failed read | stops at the first | every query runs, then the batch fails |
| order | input order | input order |

Neither logs; the CLI times its own commands. `Result<Vec<Hits>>` rather than `Vec<Result<Hits>>` because a failed read is a file problem, not a query problem, and every caller collected into it anyway.

The escape hatch is `search` for one query plus the fact that `SuffixArray` is `Send + Sync`, pinned by a test with `fn assert_sync<T: Sync>()`. A caller with its own rayon pool uses `pool.install(|| sa.par_search_all(..))`; one with its own threads uses `std::thread::scope` and `search`.

## Call sites

- `sufr/src/lib.rs`: `count`, `locate` and `extract` call `par_search_all` and drop the `collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()`.
- `libsufr/src/lib.rs` and `search.rs` tests: `search_all`.
- `libsufr/examples/search.rs`: both.

## Rejected

- Deleting the batch function and leaving parallelism to the CLI. Jack wants the library to offer it, with the serial form beside it.
- One function with a flag, or one calling the other through a one-thread pool. Two four-line functions.
- The name `search_many`. `search_all` is already on the board.
